mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with a partial offset from residential construction, resulting in muted but positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -3% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that raises wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflation surprise, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly for three months) without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1 flat) signals a savings-driven environment that depresses corporate revenue growth and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5% for three months AND GDPC1 monthly growth ≈ 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of rising income with flat consumption.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals a rapid deterioration in labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.0% in one month (vs previous month)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE jumps above 6% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a residential construction boom that boosts demand for materials and labor, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-trend housing starts.
